questions.question: Which Hungarian-British author won the 2025 Booker Prize for his novel ‘Flesh’, becoming the first person of his nationality to receive this prestigious literary award?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**David Szalay.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **Hungarian-British author David Szalay won the 2025 Booker Prize for his novel ‘Flesh’, marking the first time a Hungarian-British writer has received the honour.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **‘Flesh’ explores themes of class, power, intimacy, migration, and masculinity through the life of a man navigating between Hungary and London.**
 
• **T**he novel is noted for its spare prose, focusing on minimalism and emotional precision.
 
• The Booker Prize 2025 award ceremony was held in London, where David Szalay received £50,000 as the winner.
 
• Szalay was previously shortlisted for the 2016 Booker Prize for his novel ‘All That Man Is’.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **David Szalay:**__

 __
 
• Nationality: Hungarian-British
 
• Born: 1974 in Montreal, Canada
 
• Notable Works: ‘All That Man Is’, ‘Spring’, ‘London and the South-East’
 
• Awards: Betty Trask Prize (2008), Geoffrey Faber Memorial Prize (2009)
 
 
 
• **The Booker Prize:**__
 __
 
• One of the most prestigious literary awards for fiction written in English.
 
• Founded in 1969, awarded annually in London.
 
• Prize Money: £50,000 to the winner and £2,500 to each shortlisted author and translator.
 
 
 
• **Judging Panel (2025):**__ Chaired by Roddy Doyle, who praised ‘Flesh’ for its unique use of white space and narrative depth.
 
• __**Past Winners:**__ Salman Rushdie, Margaret Atwood, Hilary Mantel, Arundhati Roy, and Kazuo Ishiguro are among the notable Booker laureates.

questions.question: The FIDE Chess World Cup 2025 trophy unveiled in Goa has been named after which chess legend?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Viswanathan Anand.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **The new FIDE Chess World Cup trophy unveiled in Goa has been named the Viswanathan Anand Trophy__, in honour of the five-time World Champion.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The trophy is named after Viswanathan Anand__, India’s five-time World Chess Champion and a global chess icon.**
 
• The trophy was unveiled during the opening ceremony of the FIDE Chess World Cup 2025 held in Panjim, Goa.
 
• The Viswanathan Anand Trophy is a __rolling trophy__ that will be passed on to future World Cup champions.
 
• The ceremony was attended by senior dignitaries including Union Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya and FIDE President Arkady Dvorkovich.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Viswanathan Anand:**__ An Indian chess grandmaster, former World Chess Champion (multiple formats), and one of the most influential figures in modern chess; credited with popularising chess in India and inspiring a generation of players.
 
• __**Rolling Trophy:**__ A perpetual or rotating trophy awarded to each tournament winner for the year; the trophy is returned to the organisers and passed to the next champion, creating a continuous legacy.
 
• __**FIDE (Fédération Internationale des Échecs):**__ The international governing body of chess responsible for organizing world championships, rating players, and overseeing international chess regulations and events.
 
• __**AICF (All India Chess Federation):**__ The national governing body for chess in India responsible for promoting the sport domestically and coordinating with FIDE for international events hosted in India.
 
• __**Bye in Round 1:**__ A tournament provision where higher-seeded players skip the initial round(s) and automatically advance to the next stage; used to balance draws when participant counts do not form perfect brackets.
 
• __**Top Seed / Seeded Player:**__ A competitor ranked highest entering a tournament; seedings are used to structure the draw so that top players do not meet in early rounds.
 
• __**Draw of Colours:**__ The process determining which player starts with white or black pieces in a match; starting with white is often considered advantageous since white moves first.
 
• __**Grandmaster (GM):**__ The highest title awarded by FIDE to chess players, signifying elite international standard of play.
 
• __**Chess Olympiad:**__ A biennial international team chess event where national teams compete; winning Olympiad titles is a major national achievement, often cited when assessing a country’s chess progress.

questions.question: Who has been nominated as the next Executive Chairman of the National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) in November 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Justice Vikram Nath.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__** 

__
 
• **Supreme Court judge Justice Vikram Nath has been nominated as the next Executive Chairman of the National Legal Services Authority (NALSA).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__** 

__
 
• **Justice Vikram Nath will assume charge as Executive Chairman of NALSA from November 24, 2025.**
 
• **He has been serving as a Supreme Court judge since 2021.**
 
• **The nomination was made by President Droupadi Murmu under Clause (b) of Section 3(2) of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.**
 
• **He succeeds Justice Surya Kant, who has recently been sworn in as the 53rd Chief Justice of India.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

__
 
• **National Legal Services Authority (NALSA)**__

 __
 
• Established under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.
 
• Provides free and competent legal services to the weaker sections of society.
 
• Promotes legal literacy and alternative dispute resolution mechanisms like Lok Adalats.
 
 
 
• **Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987**__
 __
 
• Empowers the President to nominate a sitting Supreme Court judge as Executive Chairman of NALSA.
 
• Ensures access to justice for all citizens.
 
 
 
• **Justice Surya Kant**__
 __
 
• Previously served as Executive Chairman of NALSA.
 
• Sworn in as the 53rd Chief Justice of India.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Executive Chairman, NALSA**__
 
 
• Oversees legal aid programmes and access-to-justice initiatives.
 
• Ensures effective functioning of State Legal Services Authorities.

questions.question: Which state’s Gogabeel Lake has been recently designated as a Ramsar site, increasing India’s total to 94 wetlands of international importance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **Bihar’s Gogabeel Lake has been designated as a Ramsar site, raising India’s tally of wetlands of international importance to 94.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gogabeel Lake, located in Katihar district, is Bihar’s first community-managed oxbow lake situated between the Ganga and Mahananda rivers.**
 
• **With this addition, Bihar now has six Ramsar sites, ranking third after Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh.**
 
• **India remains the top country in Asia and third globally (after the UK and Mexico) with 94 Ramsar sites.**
 
• Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav announced the inclusion, noting that India added 67 sites in the last 11 years covering 13,60,805 hectar**es.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ramsar Convention**__

 __
 
• Adopted in 1971 in Ramsar, Iran, to conserve and ensure the wise use of wetlands.
 
• India is among the 172 member countries under this global treaty.
 
• Globally, there are 2,546 Ramsar sites covering critical wetland ecosystems.
 
 
 
• **Gogabeel Lake**__
 __
 
• Type: Oxbow lake formed by the meandering of rivers.
 
• Location: Katihar district, Bihar, between the Ganga and Mahananda rivers.
 
• Significance: Serves as a key floodplain and biodiversity hotspot managed by local communities.
 
 
 
• **India’s Ramsar Site Rankings**__
 
 
• 1st in Asia with 96 sites.
 
• 3rd in the world after the United Kingdom (176) and Mexico (144).
 
• Recent additions include Gokul Jalashay (Buxar) and Udaipur Jheel (West Champaran), both in Bihar.

questions.question: ISRO recently conducted a key development test under the Integrated Main Parachute Airdrop Test (IMAT) series in November 2025 for which mission?
questions.solution:
**Answer:** C. **__Gaganyaan__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• ISRO successfully conducted a crucial development test on the main parachutes for the Gaganyaan Crew Module at Babina Field Firing Range, Jhansi, as part of the Integrated Main Parachute Airdrop Test (IMAT) series on November 3, 2025.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• The test validated the parachute system’s performance under extreme conditions, including delay in disreefing between two main parachutes.
 
• The parachute system includes **10 parachutes of four types**—apex cover, drogue, pilot, and main parachutes.
 
• Reefed inflation technique ensures controlled deployment using **pyro devices** for reefing and disreefing stages.
 
• The Crew Module was simulated using a mass equivalent, dropped from an altitude of 2.5 km by an **Indian Air Force IL-76 aircraft**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The test confirmed safe descent and soft landing, validating the parachute’s structural integrity and load distribution.
 
• Developed by **Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (VSSC)** with support from **ADRDE (DRDO)**, the Indian Air Force, and the Indian Army.
 
• The IMAT series aims to qualify the parachute system for India’s first **human spaceflight mission – Gaganyaan**.

questions.question: Which country recently secured its fourth Davis Cup title by achieving a 2-0 victory over Spain and completing a historic third consecutive championship?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Italy.**__

__
 
• **Italy clinched its fourth Davis Cup title overall.**
 
• **The team became the first nation since the United States to win three consecutive Davis Cups.**
 
• **Matteo Berrettini secured the first win of the final against Pablo Carreno Busta.**
 
• **Flavio Cobolli completed the victory by defeating Jaume Munar in a three-set battle.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

__
 
• **Davis Cup**__

 __
 
• Often called the "World Cup of Tennis."
 
• Organised by the International Tennis Federation (ITF).
 
• Features national teams competing in singles and doubles matches.
 
 
 
• **Spain**__
 __
 
• Finished as runners-up in the final after a 2-0 loss to Italy.
 
• Pablo Carreno Busta and Jaume Munar represented the Spanish team in singles.
 
 
 
• **United States**__
 __
 
• Holds the record for most Davis Cup titles.
 
• Previously the only team to win three consecutive championships before Italy matched the feat.
 
 
 
• **Matteo Berrettini & Flavio Cobolli**__
 
 
• Both won their singles matches in the final to give Italy an unbeatable lead.
 
• Berrettini won in straight sets; Cobolli made a comeback in three sets.

questions.question: Bharat Electronics Limited signed a Joint Venture Cooperation Agreement with which French company for the production of the HAMMER precision-guided weapon system?

questions.question: According to the Climate Risk Index (CRI) 2026 released by Germanwatch, where does India rank globally among the countries most affected by extreme weather events between 1995 and 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**9th.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• The Climate Risk Index (CRI) 2026 released by Germanwatch ranked India 9th among the countries most affected by extreme weather events between 1995 and 2024.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• India ranked 9th in CRI 2026, highlighting long-term vulnerability to rapid-onset extreme weather events.
 
• The country recorded around 430 extreme weather incidents in the past 30 years, causing losses of approximately $170 billion.
 
• India ranked 3rd globally in terms of population affected, behind Bangladesh and the Philippines.
 
• India has been placed in the “continuous threats” category, indicating repeated and frequent climate disasters.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Climate Risk Index (CRI)**__

 __
 
• Developed by Germanwatch to assess the impact of extreme weather events.
 
• Calculated based on human and economic losses.
 
• Higher the rank, the more severely a country is affected.
 
 
 
• **Rapid Onset Events Considered**__
 __
 
• Includes storms, floods, glacial lake outburst floods, extreme temperatures, and wildfires.
 
• Aims to analyse sudden climate shocks.
 
• India’s repeated exposure places it among the highest-risk nations.
 
 
 
• **Slow Onset Events (Not Included)**__
 __
 
• Rising sea levels, ocean acidification, glacial retreat, and warming trends are not part of CRI calculations.
 
• These events require long-term monitoring beyond rapid disaster assessment.
 
• Exclusion means CRI focuses only on immediate climatic impacts.
 
 
 
• **Continuous Threats Category**__
 
 
• Includes India, the Philippines, Nicaragua, and Haiti.
 
• Countries in this category face frequent and recurring extreme events.
 
• Reflects chronic vulnerability to climate-related disasters.

questions.question: The Mudh-Nyoma Air Force Station inaugurated, is located near the Line of Actual Control (LAC). How far is this high-altitude airbase situated from the LAC?
questions.solution:

__
 
• India inaugurated the Mudh-Nyoma Air Force Station in eastern Ladakh, located 23 km from the Line of Actual Control (LAC) on 12 November 2025.

• Its inauguration signifies a major boost to India’s border infrastructure following the 2020 standoff.

• **Border Roads Organisation (BRO)**__
 __

• **India-China LAC**__

questions.question: Which two countries launched the 11ᵗʰ edition of Exercise Mitra Shakti at the Foreign Training Node in Belagavi, Karnataka, focused on counter-terrorism and peacekeeping scenarios in November 2025?

__
 
• Exercise Mitra Shakti is a recurring **bilateral military exercise** between the Indian and Sri Lankan armies aimed at enhancing **counter-terrorism, sub-conventional warfare**, and **UN peacekeeping** operational coordination.
 
• The exercise will run from **10 to 23 November 2025**, at the Foreign Training Node, Belagavi, Karnataka.
 
• Participating forces include the **Rajput Regiment** from India and the **Gajaba Regiment** from Sri Lanka, along with air force personnel from both countries.

 __

• **Key Features of Mitra Shakti XI (2025)**__
 __
 
• Training focuses on **search and destroy missions, heliborne operations**, counter-terrorist raids, combat reflex shooting, and casualty evacuation.
 
• Emphasis on **modern warfare techniques**, such as **drone and counter-drone warfare** (C-UAS).

• Edition: 11ᵗʰ

• Venue: Foreign Training Node, Belagavi, Karnataka
 
• Indian Regiment: Rajput Regiment
 
• Sri Lankan Regiment: Gajaba Regiment

questions.question: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated India’s first Digital Museum of Tribal Freedom Fighters at Nava Raipur, Atal Nagar. What is the official name of this museum dedicated to tribal heroes and their contribution to India’s freedom movement?

options.text: Shaheed Veer Narayan Singh Memorial and Tribal Freedom Fighters Museum

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shaheed Veer Narayan Singh Memorial and Tribal Freedom Fighters Museum.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated India’s first Digital Museum of Tribal Freedom Fighters, named “Shaheed Veer Narayan Singh Memorial and Tribal Freedom Fighters Museum,” at Nava Raipur, Atal Nagar, Chhattisgarh.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• The museum is India’s first fully digital museum dedicated to tribal heroes and freedom fighters.
 
• It features VFX displays, digital projections, QR-coded storytelling, and interactive touchscreens to create an immersive learning experience.
 
• It pays tribute to Shaheed Veer Narayan Singh (1820–1857), the first martyr of Chhattisgarh who led a revolt against British exploitation during the famine of 1856–57.
 
• The museum highlights various tribal uprisings** like the Halba Rebellion, Bhumkal Movement, and Jhanda & Jungle Satyagrahas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About Shaheed Veer Narayan Singh**__

 __
 
• Born: **1820** in Sonakhan, Chhattisgarh.
 
• Role: Led a peasant and tribal uprising against British grain hoarding during the famine of 1856–57.
 
• Martyrdom: Executed by the British in **1857**, becoming a symbol of tribal resistance and patriotism.
 
• Legacy: The **Veer Narayan Singh Stadium** in Raipur is named in his honour.
 
 
 
• **Major Revolts Showcased**__
 __
 
• **Halba Rebellion** – Early tribal uprising against British rule in Chhattisgarh.
 
• **Bhumkal Movement** – Revolt against British land and tax policies.
 
• **Rani Chauris Struggle** – Women-led movement against colonial oppression.
 
• **Jhanda & Jungle Satyagrahas** – Nonviolent protests for tribal rights and forest access.
 
 
 
• **Museum Significance**__
 __
 
• Combines **technology with history** to preserve tribal heritage and valor.
 
• Serves as a **hub for cultural tourism and education** in Chhattisgarh.
 
• Enhances awareness about **tribal contributions to India’s independence**.
 
 
 
• **Location Details**__
 
 
• City: **Nava Raipur, Atal Nagar**
 
• State: **Chhattisgarh**
 
• Inaugurated by: **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**

questions.question: Which Indian state became the first to sign a partnership agreement with Elon Musk’s Starlink for deploying satellite-based internet services?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maharashtra.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **Maharashtra** has become the **first Indian state** to sign a partnership agreement with **Elon Musk’s Starlink Satellite Communications Pvt Ltd** to deploy satellite-based internet services.
 
• The **Letter of Intent (LOI)** was signed between the **Maharashtra Government** and **Starlink** on **November 5, 2025**.
 
• The collaboration aims to provide **satellite-based internet connectivity** to **rural and underserved regions** of the state.
 
• Key focus areas include **Gadchiroli, Nandurbar, Washim, and Dharashiv** districts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Maharashtra** is the first Indian state to officially tie up with **Starlink** for **satellite-based digital connectivity.**
 
• The initiative aligns with the state’s **Digital Maharashtra Mission** and supports **EV infrastructure, coastal development, and disaster resilience programs.**
 
• **Starlink** operates the world’s largest constellation of communication satellites, under **SpaceX** founded by **Elon Musk.**
 
• **Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis** described the collaboration as a “giant leap toward a future-ready Maharashtra.”

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Starlink (by SpaceX)**__

 __
 
• Global satellite internet service provider by **Elon Musk’s SpaceX.**
 
• Operates a **constellation of over 6,000 satellites** in low Earth orbit (LEO).
 
• Provides high-speed broadband to remote and rural areas worldwide.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Maharashtra–Starlink Partnership**__
 __
 
• Will enable **high-speed internet access** in **remote and aspirational districts** of the state.
 
• Integrates with **Digital India** and **Digital Maharashtra** initiatives.
 
• Supports **e-governance, telemedicine, education, and disaster management.**
 
 
 
• **IN-SPACe Approval**__
 __
 
• **Indian National Space Promotion and Authorization Centre (IN-SPACe)** granted permission to Starlink to begin operations in India.
 
• This regulatory approval paved the way for **state-level partnerships** like Maharashtra’s.
 
 
 
• **Other Related Developments**__
 
 
• The collaboration positions Maharashtra as a **leader in satellite-enabled digital infrastructure** in India.
 
• It also supports the state’s long-term goals of **smart rural connectivity** and **disaster-resilient communication systems.**
